claims.statement: Regulation 2024/573 requires equipment-level records for covered leak-checked equipment, including gas quantities, service undertaking and person identity, work dates and outcomes, and retention or database availability.
EU certification requirements now cover specified stationary equipment containing F-gases and relevant alternatives including ammonia, carbon dioxide, and hydrocarbons.
Poland updated CRO in March 2024 with new equipment-card fields and coverage for specified HFO and HCFO quantities, confirming a changing structured record workflow.
UDT reported more than 14,000 Polish enterprise F-gas certificates for stationary refrigeration, air-conditioning, and heat-pump work and planned more than 3,400 enterprise inspections in 2024.
Montak already offers Polish HVAC protocols, F-gas reminders, equipment history, and recurring inspections at 0 PLN, 199 PLN, and 399 PLN monthly tiers.
Montero, Fieldworker, and Clima Pro directly market overlapping Polish mobile protocols, F-gas records, equipment histories, audit readiness, or CRO documentation.

contrary_evidence: Montak is a direct Polish substitute with a non-expiring free tier and paid tiers of 199 and 399 PLN per month, including protocols, equipment history, recurring inspections, and unlimited devices on paid plans.

Montero, Fieldworker, and Clima Pro demonstrate that mobile F-gas documentation, audit preparation, asset history, and CRO-ready workflows are already an active product category rather than whitespace.
CRO and UDT remain the authoritative registry and certification rails, so the product cannot sell authority or registry access.
The dated UDT universe of more than 14,000 certified firms makes the wealth-path example dependent on a large domestic share or cross-border expansion, neither of which is validated.

economics.acquisition_route: Use the family installer for workflow measurement, obtain 10 paid firms through one wholesaler or trainer only after a measurable pilot, and test technician-to-customer maintenance reminders before assuming operator revenue.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, not validated: 2,000 firms at 3,600 PLN ARR plus 50 operator accounts at 24,000 PLN ARR yields 8.4m PLN ARR. At 25% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, 75% founder ownership, and no double-counting of retained cash, founder equity could reach about 6.3m PLN in years 7-10. This requires material Polish share or European expansion despite established competitors.
economics.founder_time: 2.5-4 hours per day for one design-partner pilot; regulatory interpretation and onboarding must be delegated before serving more than roughly 20 firms.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Inference: 72-86% after software hosting, channel commission, onboarding, and contracted regulatory review; support-heavy audit remediation would be separately priced.
economics.payback: Unknown. A target of 12-18 months requires low-touch onboarding and channel CAC below roughly one year of gross profit; no paid conversion, churn, support-load, or channel-cost evidence exists.
economics.pricing: Validation hypothesis: 149-399 PLN per company per month, aligned with Polish vertical-software anchors; defer per-asset pricing until a pilot proves incremental value beyond existing unlimited-device plans.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Equipment histories and recurring service visits create genuine repeat use, but retention must come from scheduling, job closure, customer proof, and service revenue because regulatory forms alone are available elsewhere.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned longitudinal graph of equipment, service events, technicians, credentials, refrigerant movements, and repeat-maintenance outcomes could improve data entry and retention, although existing Polish field-service products can build similar histories
fingerprint.customer: Polish micro and small certified HVAC, refrigeration, and heat-pump installation and service firms with recurring service work; multi-site operators are a later, unvalidated segment
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Begin with the family renewable installer as design partner, then test referrals through refrigerant wholesalers, equipment distributors, and certification trainers; no channel commitment is currently evidenced
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Mobile field-service workflow with asset history, refrigerant ledger, certificate-aware checks, signed customer PDFs, recurring-service reminders, CRO-ready evidence, and audit binder sold as vertical SaaS
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The service company pays a monthly company or technician subscription when digital job closure, recurring-service reminders, and audit evidence replace paper and duplicate entry; operator payment is not yet evidenced
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A technician installs, repairs, leak-checks, recovers refrigerant from, services, or decommissions regulated equipment and the firm must preserve a consistent work record, customer proof, credential trail, and any required CRO equipment-card entry

founder_fit: The parents' renewable-energy installer provides direct, bounded design-partner access without requiring a public personal brand.
The product uses structured data, automation, and measurable field-workflow outcomes that fit the founder's skills.
A narrow prototype and one-company pilot can fit within 5 hours per day and available capital.
Scaling would require outsourced regulatory review and productised onboarding rather than founder-run compliance consulting.
risks: A compliance-led position is commoditised by existing Polish field-service products and free official workflows.
Incorrect credential, threshold, or refrigerant logic could create compliance harm and support liability.
Technician adoption may fail if data entry is not materially faster than paper or an incumbent app.
The founder's part-time constraint is incompatible with bespoke onboarding or continuous audit consulting at scale.
F-gas phase-down and equipment transitions can change which records matter, increasing maintenance cost.

structure.control_point: the technician's job-completion record from which customer evidence, recurring service, and CRO-ready data are produced
structure.critical_dependency: sufficient time saved versus low-cost Polish field-service alternatives and an accurate, maintainable transfer workflow into CRO

thesis: Test a mobile-first service-record and recurring-maintenance system for small Polish HVAC, refrigeration, and heat-pump firms, using the family installer as a bounded design partner. EU and Polish rules create recurring record, credential, equipment-card, and audit work, but the category is already served by Polish products at low prices. The viable wedge therefore cannot be a static F-gas checklist or access to CRO; it must measurably reduce technician entry, produce customer and audit evidence in the job flow, and recover repeat service revenue. CRO transfer, distributor access, and willingness to pay above existing field-service products remain unproven.
title: CRO ServiceProof for Heat-Pump and Refrigeration Firms
uncertainties: Whether CRO offers a supported integration mechanism or requires assisted manual transfer.
Whether a small installer will pay for this product instead of Montak, Montero, Fieldworker, Clima Pro, paper, or the public portal.
Which workflow produces enough measured time saving or repeat-service revenue to support paid conversion.
Whether wholesalers, distributors, or trainers will distribute independent software and on what economics.
Current numbers of active certified firms, covered assets, and multi-site operators willing to buy portfolio oversight.
